phrases.text: Imagine you land in a shiny desert city for the job of your dreams
The salary is tax-free the housing is free and there's money to send home every month
At the airport your new boss greets you with a big smile
Let me keep your passport he says
For safekeeping
And you're thinking
Wow that's actually kind of nice
At first it's paradise
Air-conditioned malls glass skyscrapers and your family back home telling everyone you've made it
Then your first salary comes a little late
Paperwork he says
The second one is late too
The job you're doing isn't the job you signed up for and the room you were promised has eleven other guys in it
So you decide to quit
Easy right
Except your visa is tied to him and so is your right to stay in the country
If you just walk out he can report you for absconding and suddenly you're the criminal
So you decide to go home instead
You walk up to the airport counter and the officer asks you one question
Passport
Your passport is sitting in a drawer in your boss's office
Every Friday you call your mother and tell her everything's great because you still owe the recruitment agent back home more than you've earned
But the guy on the bunk above you has been here nine years and sends money home every month like clockwork
So you keep your head down and do the same
Then one morning his bunk is empty
His bag is gone and nobody will tell you whether he went home or just disappeared
Taking a worker's passport is actually illegal in most of these countries
But a law doesn't do much when nobody enforces it
They never had to lock the door
They just took the one thing you need to walk through it
